## Terms

### index

- **index** · self — Index prefixes are the beginning subsets of indexed fields. Compound indexes support queries on all fields included in the index prefix. · aka: indexes, indices, indexing, indexed — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-compound/#index-prefixes

### compound index

- **compound index** · hyponym — Compound indexes may contain **a single** [hashed index field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed/#std-label-index-type-hashed) · aka: compound indexes, composite index, composite indexes, multi-column index, multicolumn index · MongoDB 'compound' = SQL 'composite'/'multicolumn' — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-compound/#hashed-index-fields

### unique index

- **unique index** · hyponym — Unique indexes ensure that a value appears at most once for a given field. · aka: unique indexes, uniqueIndex — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/create/#chunk-0

### partial index

- **partial index** · hyponym — The `where` argument allows you to define [partial indexes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-partial.html) (also known as filtered indexes). A partial index only includes rows that match a specified condition, which reduces the index size and improves both write performance and query  · aka: partial indexes, filtered index, partialIndexes — https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/indexes#configuring-partial-indexes-with-where-configuring-partial-indexes-with-where

### B-tree

- **B-tree** · hyponym — * B-trees are versatile and widely applicable: * **Equality and Range Queries**: They excel in handling equality and range queries. Common operators include `=`, `<`, `>`, `BETWEEN`, and `IN`. * **NULL Conditions**: B-trees can handle `IS NULL` or `IS NOT NULL` conditions. * **Pattern Matching**: Wh · aka: btree, B+tree, b-tree index, B-tree indexes — https://thenile.dev/docs/postgres/indexes#b-tree-index

### GIN index

- **GIN index** · hyponym — * GIN indexes can be large, plan storage accordingly * Index creation might be slow for large tables * Index only necessary columns * Monitor index size and search performance * Adjust similarity threshold to balance precision and recall * Consider using `pg_bigm.enable_recheck` for better accuracy · aka: GIN, GIN indexes, generalized inverted index, gin_trgm_ops · Postgres — https://thenile.dev/docs/extensions/pg_bigm#performance-considerations

### GiST index

- **GiST index** · hyponym — GiST indexes are a versatile type of index that can handle complex data types, such as geometric shapes, full-text search, and network addresses. [They are implemented using a custom data structure optimized for searching large amounts of data1](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/gist.html). He · aka: GiST, SP-GiST, GiST indexes, btree_gist · Postgres — https://thenile.dev/docs/postgres/indexes#gist-index

### BRIN index

- **BRIN index** · hyponym · aka: BRIN, block range index, BRIN indexes · Postgres

### hashed index

- **hashed index** · hyponym — Hashed indexes support [hashed sharding](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/hashed-sharding/#std-label-sharding-hashed-sharding). Hashed indexes index the hash of a field's value. · aka: hashed indexes, hash index, hash indexes, $toHashedIndexKey — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/#chunk-2

### text index

- **text index** · hyponym — Text indexes tokenize and stem the terms in the indexed fields for the index entries. The index uses simple [language-specific](https://www.mongodb.com#std-label-text-index-supported-languages) suffix stemming. For each document in the collection, the text index stores one index entry for each uniqu · aka: text indexes, full-text index, search index, search indexes, withSearchIndex, tsvector, pg_trgm · full-text/search indexes (Atlas Search, Convex search index, Postgres FTS) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/text-index-properties/#index-entries

### vector index

- **vector index** · hyponym — * Vector index works only for tables **with** `ROWID` or with singular `PRIMARY KEY`. Composite `PRIMARY KEY` without `ROWID` is not supported · aka: vector indexes, HNSW, IVFFlat, DiskANN, vectorIndex, approximate nearest neighbor · pgvector / Atlas Vector Search / Convex vector index — an index type, not the Pinecone sense — https://docs.turso.tech/features/ai-and-embeddings#index-limitations

### multikey index

- **multikey index** · hyponym — Multikey indexes are used for arrays of values within documents. · aka: multikey, multikey indexes — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/llms.txt

### TTL index

- **TTL index** · hyponym · aka: TTL indexes, expireAfterSeconds

### wildcard index

- **wildcard index** · hyponym — Wildcard indexes can support a [covered query](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/#std-label-covered-queries) only if **all** of the following conditions are true: · aka: wildcard indexes — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-wildcard/#covered-queries

### geospatial index

- **geospatial index** · hyponym — Geospatial indexes support queries involving location-based data. · aka: geospatial indexes, 2dsphere, 2d index — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/llms.txt

### clustered index

- **clustered index** · hyponym — Clustered indexes specify the order in which [clustered collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/#std-label-clustered-collections) store data. Collections created with a clustered index are called clustered collections. · aka: clustered indexes, clustered collection, WITHOUT ROWID — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/#chunk-3

### expression index

- **expression index** · hyponym — An expression index stores the result of an expression rather than a raw column value. Use expression indexes when queries frequently filter or sort by a computed value. · aka: expression indexes, functional index, index on an expression — https://docs.turso.tech/sql-reference/statements/create-index#expression-indexes

### sparse index

- **sparse index** · hyponym · aka: sparse indexes

### hidden index

- **hidden index** · hyponym — Hidden indexes are not visible to the [query planner](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans/) and cannot be used to support a query. · aka: hidden indexes, hideIndex, unhideIndex — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/#chunk-0

### index definition

- **index definition** · part · aka: index name, index fields, index key, index keys, key pattern, index entry, index entries, index bounds, index specification, IndexFields, IndexName

### index prefix

- **index prefix** · part — Index prefixes are the beginning subsets of indexed fields. Compound indexes support queries on all fields included in the index prefix. · aka: index prefixes, leftmost prefix, left-most prefix, prefix of the index, leading column — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-compound/#index-prefixes

### covered query

- **covered query** · dependent · aka: covered queries, covering index, covering indexes, index-only scan, index only scan, covered by an index, cover multiple queries

### ESR rule

- **ESR rule** · dependent · aka: ESR guideline, ESR, equality sort range, Equality, Sort, Range

### index build

- **index build** · dependent — [Index Builds on Populated Collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/) for more information on the behavior of indexing operations in MongoDB. · aka: index builds, CREATE INDEX, createIndex, createIndexes, DROP INDEX, dropIndex, dropIndexes, CONCURRENTLY, index creation, create an index, add an index, drop an index, rolling index build, staged index, getIndexes, listIndexes, index backfill — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/reIndex/#tip

### @@index

### withIndex

- **withIndex** · instance — `.withIndex` is designed to only allow you to specify ranges that Convex can efficiently use your index to find. For all other filtering you can use the [`.filter`](/api/interfaces/server.Query.md#filter) method. · aka: IndexRangeBuilder, index range, range expression, .index(, IndexRange, LowerBoundIndexRangeBuilder · Convex index API — file:///Users/mitch/.global-ai-hub/llms-full/files/docs.convex.dev.txt#querying-documents-using-indexes-querying-documents-using-indexes-direct-link-to-querying-documents-using-indexes

### selectivity

- **selectivity** · measure — Selectivity is a query property that describes the ratio of documents matching the query versus the total number of documents in a collection. The selectivity of an index describes how many documents a unique index key matches. A query or index has high selectivity when proportionally few documents  · aka: selective, cardinality, high-cardinality, planner statistics, sqlite_stat1, n_distinct, pg_stats — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/create-queries-that-ensure-selectivity/#chunk-0

### query planner

- **query planner** · whole — Hidden indexes are not visible to the [query planner](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans/) and cannot be used to support a query. · aka: query optimizer, planner, optimizer, winningPlan, rejectedPlans, plan cache — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/#chunk-0

### explain plan

- **explain plan** · related — Explain plan results for queries are subject to change between MongoDB versions. · aka: explain(), EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, query plan, execution plan, explain output, explain results, explain("executionStats"), explain plans — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/#note
